office_does: The District 3 commissioner is one of three members of the Board of County Commissioners, which passes county ordinances, adopts the budget, sets land use and oversees county departments; nominated by District 3 (eastern county), elected county-wide, four-year term.
race_blurb: Republican Asa Leckie, the board's chair and an Army Special Forces veteran elected in 2022, faces Democrat Paul H. Mosbrucker of Underwood, a former school board member. Leckie led the district primary 775 to 629 and runs on no new taxes, timber revenue and pushing back on state mandates; Mosbrucker points to housing costs, insurance premiums, school cuts and slow job growth and asks for new leadership.

candidates.summary: District 3 commissioner, elected in 2022, and board chair; an Army Special Forces veteran of more than two decades from Carson, running for re-election as a Republican.
highlights: Says he has never voted for or supported the county's annual 1% property tax increase [S1]
Wants core-services budgets 'without unnecessary tax increases' [S2]
Proposes logging along Gifford Pinchot roads and payments to counties for conservation set-asides [S3]
Voted to open about 400 acres in Underwood to 10-acre residential lots [S4]
Joined the board's opposition to 77,000 acres of new state legacy forests [S5]

taxes.basis: 'We're taxed enough already': says he has never voted for the county's 1% levy increase and wants budgets without tax increases, stated in the pamphlet and the Chamber Q&A.

spending.basis: Calls for 'fiscal discipline' and budgets that prioritize core services, while also backing public-private partnerships and business incentives where feasible.

housing.basis: Treats the shortage of developable land as the housing constraint and voted to zone previously unzoned Underwood forest land for 10-acre residential lots over neighbors' objections; no public-housing or tenant position.

climate.basis: Wants to 'reduce energy costs' and expand timber harvest, and opposed state legacy-forest set-asides, but states no position on carbon pricing or clean-energy policy.

experience.basis: Sitting commissioner and board chair running on his record in office.

candidates.summary: Underwood resident of 22 years and former White Salmon Valley School District board member; running as a Democrat on his first county campaign.
highlights: Names scarce, unaffordable housing, insurance premiums, school cuts and slow job growth as the county's problems [S1]
Says the county budget is 'at the mercy of politicians who don't live here' [S1]
Calls for 'new leadership and innovative ideas' [S1]
Raised $4,971 by Sept. 28, including $1,500 from the county Democrats [S4][S5]

experience.basis: Runs explicitly for 'new leadership' against the board chair and has held no county office, though he cites management experience and past school board service.
